Carbon closure per process

The model has no carbon balance constraint. Where its coefficients do not conserve carbon, the process is outlined in red in the diagram.

How to read it

Each box is a bus or a technology of the model. Each line is a route that carbon can take. The diagram shows which routes exist, not how much carbon flows; the optimiser chooses among them.

Sources and sinks

Carbon enters with the digester feedstock, bought biomass and natural gas. It leaves as biomethane, methanol, liquid CO₂, biochar, digestate to the fields, or CO₂ to the air.

Outside the model

Upstream emissions, such as field emissions, manure storage, transport and methane slip, are not included.

How carbon is counted

Only CO₂ and biochar buses carry tonnes in the network. Methane and methanol are in MWh, biomass in MWh or t DM. Their carbon follows from the coefficients in the table below, taken from the same technology-data year, workbook and stream properties as the network.

The biogas bus holds methane energy only. Its CO₂ share is implicit and appears when biogas is upgraded, burned or converted.

What is not in the model

The digestate carbon fraction is an assumption of this page. The model tracks digestate as dry matter only, and the feedstock carbon is set so the digester closes.

Upstream emissions (fields, manure storage, transport) and methane slip are outside the system boundary.

Presets

Presets carry the annual flows of solved tutorial networks. Regenerate them with python docs/_static/model/generate_carbon_data.py, optionally with --network NAME=path.nc for your own run.
